item.title: G.R.H. Polymath
item.description: [This is a guest post by Anurag Sahai, Will Sawin, and Lior Silberman – T.] Last Friday Levent Alpöge announced a Lean certicate containing a proof of the Generalized Riemann hypothesis. Since then there has been a flurry of activity in validating the certificate, and toward extracting a human-understnable proof and simplifying the Lean certificate […]

item.title: Counting elliptic curves by discriminant
item.description: We prove an asymptotic formula with a power saving for the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ ordered by minimal discriminant, assuming the $abc$ conjecture. Unconditionally, we obtain the same asymptotic for the curves with $|\Delta_{\min}(E)| \le X$ and $c_4(E) \le X^{8/3 - \delta}$ for any fixed $\delta > 0$, by obtaining new bounds for the number of integral points $(c_4, c_6)$ near the cusp $c_4^3 = c_6^2$.

item.title: Matrix Criteria for Mordell--Weil Ranks of Quartic Twists of $y^2=x^3+x$ with Root Number $-1$
item.description: We study the Mordell--Weil ranks of quartic twists $E_a:y^2=x^3+ax$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with global root number $-1$. For $D$ a product of $n\ge2$ distinct odd primes, a $2$-isogeny descent yields unconditional rank bounds for $E_D$, $E_{-D}$, and $E_{-2D}$ in terms of matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by additive Legendre symbols. Under suitable congruence and matrix-rank conditions, these curves have rank at most one, and rank one assuming the Mordell--Weil parity conjecture. For $E_{-2D}$, an additional explicit square condition establishes rank one unconditionally. Our results extend earlier two-prime criteria to arbitrary numbers of prime factors and further to fourth-power-free coefficients $H=\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i^{e_i}$, where $e_i\in\{1,3\}$.

item.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
item.description: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

item.title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
item.description: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.

item.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
item.description: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.

item.title: The Residual Unitary Case for Almost Elusive Groups
item.description: In this short note, we remove the residual unitary family in Hall's classification of almost elusive classical groups and the corresponding conditional family in the quasiprimitive classification. Using theorems of Zsigmondy and Schinzel together with some elementary number theory arguments, we prove that if n > 4 is odd, f > 1 is even, and r is the unique primitive prime divisor of (2^f)^{2n} - 1, then 4nf divides r - 1. For n > 4 prime and any positive integer f, we deduce that a unique primitive prime divisor r of (2^f)^{2n} - 1 satisfies r > 4nf, except when (n, f, r) = (5, 1, 11). We then obtain two conjugacy classes of derangements of the same prime order in a broader family of unitary subspace actions, and a quadratic lower bound for the number of such classes in the corresponding product actions.

item.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
item.description: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

item.title: Counting solutions to Euclidean Fermat equations
item.description: A solution $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^3-\{(0,0,0)\}$ to a Fermat equation \begin{equation} \label{eq:abstract-gfe} Ax^a + By^b + Cz^c = 0 \end{equation} is called \emph{primitive} if $\gcd(x,y,z) = 1$. In the \emph{Euclidean} regime (that is, when the Euler characteristic $\chi = \tfrac{1}{a} + \tfrac{1}{b} + \tfrac{1}{c} - 1$ is zero), the equation above defines a smooth genus one curve in a weighted projective plane. We study these models and provide an asymptotic formula for the number of primitive integral solutions with bounded height.

item.title: Minor--Skein Spatial Negami Splitting Vectors and a Gluing Formula for Marked State Sums
item.description: We organize the edge states of a decorated spatial graph by the minors of their underlying abstract graphs. For pieces with disjoint edge sets, Negami's component formula and functorial ribbon evaluation express each marked sector as a boundary pairing, provided the local data determine its marker. We give two explicit rules for this last step. A two-terminal rule for $3$-connected targets tests each piece with and without a virtual edge. At arbitrary finite vertex boundaries, records of partial branch sets determine the occurrence of each fixed simple target. The rules assign a weight once per edge state, even when the state contains several minor models.

item.title: Ramsey numbers of fixed-length cycles, paths and stars in set-colored triple systems
item.description: Let $R_3(H;r,s,t)$ be the least order of a complete triple system in which every assignment of $s$ of $r$ colors to each triple forces a copy of $H$ whose edges share at least $t$ colors. Fix $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$ and let $n$ count edges. We prove that the Ramsey numbers of the linear path and the linear cycle of fixed length $n$ are both $\gamma n+o(n)$ as $n\to\infty$, with $\gamma=2$ if and only if $r=s$. For tight paths the corresponding formula is $\tau n+o(n)$, with the same coefficient for tight cycles when $3\mid n$. To obtain exactly $n$ edges in a linear cycle, we choose the parity of the connections and vary the lengths of the paths they join. For a linear star $S_n$, whose edges meet only at the center, $R_3(S_n;r,s,t)=cn+O(n^{2/3})$ for fixed colors. For fixed $n\ge2$ and $s,t$ as $r\to\infty$, it is asymptotic to $\sqrt{6a_n\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}}$, where $a_n=n(n-1)$ for odd $n$ and $a_n=n(2n-3)/2$ for even $n$. For a tight star, whose edges share a pair, the leading term is $(n-1)\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$ in both regimes. For a fixed linear path of $n\ge3$ edges and fixed $s\ge t\ge2$, the upper bound is $(2000h/1307+o

item.title: Power-Law Lower Bounds for Edges in Odd Induced Subgraphs
item.description: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $g(G)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an induced subgraph of $G$ in which every vertex has odd degree. Motivated by Scott's question of whether $g(G) \geq cm$ for every graph with $m$ edges, we prove that $g(G) \geq cm^{4/7}$ for every finite simple graph with $m \geq 1$ edges, where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant. For bipartite graphs, we obtain the stronger bound $g(B) \geq cm^{2/3}$.

item.title: Bounds for the small Davenport constant of extraspecial groups of exponent three
item.description: Let $E_s$ be the extraspecial group of order $3^{2s+1}$ and exponent three. We prove $4s+2r+2\le d(E_s\times C_3^r)\le 4s+2r+3$ for $s\ge1$ and $r\ge0$. For $s\ge2$, the degree in the polynomial proof is optimal among weights depending only on group-element multiplicities modulo three. For $s=2$, we reduce the question in all ranks to an abelian subset-sum problem with a fixed set of forbidden values in a $77$-dimensional space. We show that this set, together with zero, contains no $76$-dimensional subspace. The equality $d(E_2\times C_3^r)=2r+10$ in all ranks is not established here.

item.title: Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game
item.description: Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$. For $\{3,6,17\}$ we determine both least periods and preperiods for every positive $c$ and verify the complete table in Lean. Fixed bases with the same entire Grundy sequence realize infinitely many distinct positive quadratic coefficients for the augmented period. A second fixed triple gives a quadratic Grundy preperiod while the win/loss sequence repeats from heap zero. A third has a quadratic Grundy period but only a linear win/loss period. For an arbitrary fixed $S$, a linear bound on both Grundy invariants implies eventual affine formulas with integer coefficients on residue classes. The same finite-state method extends four numerical tables of Zhang. We also give the entire augmented sequence for $c>\max S$ when the losing heaps of $S$ are exactly the multiples of a fixe

item.title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
item.description: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$, where $L(\lambda)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(\lambda)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we give a filtration of the top homology of the mirabolic Steinberg variety in which each graded piece is a Pak--Postnikov $S_n \times S_n$-representations.

item.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
item.description: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

item.title: Major progress on hamiltonian saturation in hypergraphs
item.description: For $1\leq \ell< k$, an \emph{$\ell$-overlapping $k$-cycle} is a $k$-uniform hypergraph in which, for some cyclic vertex ordering, every edge consists of $k$ consecutive vertices and every two consecutive edges share exactly $\ell$ vertices. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is $\ell$-\emph{hamiltonian saturated} if $H$ does not contain an $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton $k$-cycle but every hypergraph obtained from $H$ by adding a new edge does contain such a cycle. For $n$ divisible by $k-\ell$, let sat$(n,k,\ell)$ be the smallest number of edges in an $\ell$-hamiltonian saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. In the case of graphs Clark and Entringer showed in 1983 that, for sufficiently large $n$, sat$(n,2,1)=\lceil \frac{3n}2\rceil$. By ad hoc methods, the present authors proved previously that sat$(n,k,\ell)=\Theta(n^{\ell})$ for some rather narrow and scattered ranges of $\ell$. In this paper we present a unified proof of this equality for all $k$ and $\ell>k/2$.

item.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
item.description: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.

item.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
item.description: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.

item.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
item.description: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.

item.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
item.description: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

item.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
item.description: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.

item.title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
item.description: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ng\^o support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms. We relate the full-base Ng\^o string to the BPS formula for intersection Hodge numbers in every rank and give the genus-two rank-three Hodge table. The arguments developed here are presented for mathematical checking and revision by the authors. And the article is generated by ChatGPT, the author is trying his best to comprehense the article and the human's version is coming soon.

item.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
item.description: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.

item.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
item.description: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.

item.title: Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
item.description: We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. If one conditions on a large deviation event in the far upper tail, the conditioned process follows the Langevin diffusion suggested by the Donsker-Varadhan variational formula for additive functionals. In contrast, if one conditions on a large deviation event in the near upper tail, the conditioned process follows a different Langevin diffusion on a fraction of the time interval and subsequently behaves like the unconditioned process. We establish this phase transition via a new sharp large deviation result for the occupation measure, which is of independent interest. We also provide further corollaries of this result and discuss generalizations to other Markov processes and additive functionals.

item.title: An easy proof of transience of one-dimensional Rademacher walk with power weights
item.description: Using a version of a local limit theorem, we provide an easy proof that the Rademacher random walk with step sizes $n^\alpha$, $\alpha>1/2$, is transient.

item.title: An $O(n^{-1/2})$ remainder for the Chow--Robbins stopping boundary
item.description: We sharpen the asymptotic approximation to the optimal stopping boundary in the Chow--Robbins game, proving the inverse-square-root remainder conjectured by Elton. The proof combines an exactly harmonic integral for simple random walk with a Catalan first-passage renewal identity. Averaging the stopping defect over one spatial period removes its leading lattice dependence, and a coupling of states at equal depth transfers this cancellation to the renewal sum. Consequently, the explicit integer stopping rule can fail at no more than a constant times the square root of the number of observation times.

item.title: Frieze's $\zeta(3)$ and the Avram--Bertsimas constant under Haar conjugation
item.description: Let $H_d=U_d^*\Lambda_dU_d$, where $U_d$ is Haar unitary and $\Lambda_d$ is a deterministic real diagonal matrix, and put $\sigma_d^2=\mathbb E|H_{12}|^2$. For minimum spanning trees with edge weights $\exp(-s|H_{ij}|^2/\sigma_d^2)$, we prove that the normalized expected weights differ from those of the independent Gaussian model by a polynomially small error, uniformly for $0 0$. The limit is the classical Avram--Bertsimas constant and includes Frieze's $\zeta(3)$ at $s=1$. For edge weights $|H_{ij}|^{-1}$, we approximate the normalized expected weight by an explicit one-dimensional integral with polynomial error, and obtain a divergent expansion in inverse powers of $\log d$. The assumptions require the spectrum, after centering and division by its standard deviation, to remain uniformly bounded. From Penrose's high-dimensional edge-length limit we derive $2-\gamma-\zeta(2)$ as the first correction to the high-dimensional Euclidean minimum spanning tree constant after normalization by the unit-ball volume. This correction is a logarithmic moment of the limiting distribution of MST edge weights; half of it is the first logarithmic co

item.title: From invasion to replacement: excursions of the Moran model
item.description: An excursion-theoretic description of the continuous-time Moran model with recurrent mutation is developed. Exploiting its birth--death structure, the killed Moran process is characterized through its Green function, resolvent, Laplace transforms of hitting times, and spectral decomposition. A duality between the Moran model and a pure-death process is also established, yielding a spectral representation of its transition probabilities. The characterization of the killed process leads to a boundary-switching excursion representation in which returning excursions correspond to unsuccessful invasions of an allelic type, whilst switching excursions describe population-wide allelic replacement. The resulting regenerative structure provides the exact joint distribution and Laplace transforms for several path statistics, including the number, height and duration of unsuccessful invasions preceding replacement. Using Doob h-transforms, convergence of the rescaled Moran excursion measures and associated point processes, restricted to excursions exceeding a fixed positive height, to their Wright--Fisher counterparts is established. These trans

item.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
item.description: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^\beta$ Poincar\'e

item.title: Concentration of the half-space Airy line ensembles
item.description: The half-space Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{hs};\varpi}$ ($\varpi\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$), introduced in arXiv:2505.01798, arXiv:2601.04546, are natural analogues of the Airy line ensemble and are expected to arise as universal scaling limits of models in the half-space Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) class. We prove that, at each fixed time $t\geq 0$, the height of the $k$th curve concentrates about $-(3\pi k/2)^{2/3}$ on the scale $k^{-1/3}\sqrt{\log(2+k)}$, with exponential tails.

item.title: Analysis and Optimal Approximation of Operator-Valued Riccati Equations with Unbounded Control Operators
item.description: In this work, we present new results on the well-posedness and approximation of the operator-valued Riccati equations that arise in the context of control systems with unbounded control operators, e.g. interior point and boundary control systems. We first prove that the Bochner integral form of the operator-valued Riccati equation is well-posed even if the control operator is unbounded. We then leverage the favorable structure of the Bochner integral form to prove that the error of approximate solutions are bounded by the approximation error of the process $C_0$-semigroup. This general result then leads to the correct prediction of optimal error estimates for the finite element approximation of the Riccati equation. The analysis is carried out on both the time-dependent and stationary Riccati equations and our numerical convergence study on the weakly damped wave process and the thermal process with delta function actuation operators corroborate the results of our analysis.

item.title: A decoupled BDF2-type integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert system in ferromagnetic multilayers
item.description: We propose and analyze a fully discrete, linear, decoupled BDF2-type finite element integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (SDLLG) system arising in spintronics. The SDLLG equations couple the magnetization dynamics with a diffusion equation for spin accumulation. The proposed numerical method combines a projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization of the magnetization dynamics with BDF2 time-stepping for the spin accumulation. By treating the coupling terms explicitly through extrapolation, each time step requires only two independent linear solves that can be performed in parallel. The analysis accommodates the usual exchange field and a general, possibly nonlinear, lower-order effective field. Unconditional weak convergence towards a global weak solution is shown. We also establish bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint. Under additional assumptions on the associated energy functional, an energy inequality for the limiting solution is obtained. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

item.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
item.description: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nystr\"om approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

item.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
item.description: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $\delta^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{

item.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
item.description: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are

item.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
item.description: The inf-sup constant $\beta(\Omega)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $\beta$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $\beta$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $\beta$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1\pi$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\le\beta\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\le\beta\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\le\beta\le

item.title: Gradient-free MCMC exploiting low-dimensional Gaussian and nonGaussian posterior structure
item.description: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian inverse problems is expensive: the unknown is high-dimensional, every likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve, and gradients are often unavailable. The posterior typically differs from the prior in a few directions and is often approximately Gaussian in most of them but strongly non-Gaussian in a few. We propose the NQU sampler, a gradient-free MCMC method that splits the parameter space into non-Gaussian (N), approximately quadratic (Q) and uninformative (U) directions. The split is learned once, before sampling, from likelihood values, and each block is updated by a kernel suited to it; a collapsed update handles a global prior scale. Because the learned structure only shapes the proposals, every update leaves the exact posterior invariant, at the cost of one likelihood evaluation. We give a condition under which the blocks can be learned and show that, for likelihoods with exactly the learned structure, the spectral gap of the sampler does not depend on the dimension, whereas updating the scale given all coordinates can have a gap of order $1/d$. On the posterior axes, the NQU sam

item.title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
item.description: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

item.title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NSOP$_1$ groups
item.description: We prove the Idempotent Measure Conjecture for type-definable groups in theories whose Keisler randomization is NSOP$_1$. More precisely, every global idempotent frequency interpretation measure on such a group is the unique left-invariant and the unique right-invariant measure concentrating on its type-definable stabilizer. In particular, its support is a left-simple convolution semigroup and has a unique minimal left ideal. The announced theorem of Ben Yaacov, Chernikov and Ramsey that randomization preserves NSOP$_1$ (proof in the appendix) yields the corresponding conclusion for all type-definable groups in NSOP$_1$ theories.

item.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
item.description: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).

item.title: Provability of Consistency: A New Foundational Landscape
item.description: This paper surveys recent developments on the provability of consistency. For nearly a century, the Unprovability of Consistency Thesis (UCT) has held that sufficiently rich systems, such as Peano Arithmetic (PA), cannot formalize a proof of their own consistency. Recent studies show that the standard G\"odelian consistency formula, Con_PA, on which the UCT argument rests, represents a non-equivalent redefinition of the original Hilbertian notion of consistency. We construct a rigorous mathematical proof of the Hilbertian consistency of PA that is formalizable within PA itself, thereby refuting UCT. While G\"odelian consistency formulas remain indispensable for comparing the relative strengths of theories, Hilbertian consistency enables internal self-verification. Beyond vindicating Hilbert's consistency program, these findings dismantle the Lucas-Penrose argument and remove perceived logical barriers to self-verifying Automated Theorem Proving and Artificial Intelligence.

item.title: Cardinal Transfer Events for Infinitary Logic with Infinitary Quantification
item.description: Assuming the existence of a certain theory $\Phi$, we solve the Gap-$n$ problem for more than one predicate. This will be done for infinitary logic with infinitary quantification.

item.title: Density elimination for weakly commutative pseudo-uninorm logic:a correction and an explicit theory-level completeness proof
item.description: We correct the density-elimination argument for weakly commutative pseudo-uninorm logic in Wang, \emph{Symmetry} 11 (2019), 368, retaining its basic ideas and overall strategy. The published definition of a labelled copy permits independent renamings of antecedent and succedent labels. Under the syntactic splicing interpretation used in that argument, a contraction-free derivable hypersequent and a four-element residuated chain refute the claimed compatibility of the resulting contraction with ordered density elimination. We require a single renaming on both sides of each closed block and prove that the linear rules and coherent closed-block contraction preserve provability of every member of the associated Cartesian families. An occurrence-based separation argument, together with normalization to cuts on the monoidal unit, establishes strong density elimination. We then derive standard completeness from density, retaining the original conclusion for formula theorems. item.title: The Borel Topos
item.description: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.

item.title: Some conservativity results for weak arithmetic theories in a language with exponentiation
item.description: Recall that $\mathsf{IOpen}$ denotes the theory of quantifier-free induction in the pure arithmetic language. In this paper, we consider an extension of $\mathsf{IOpen}$ in the arithmetical language expanded by the unary function $\exp: x \mapsto 2^x$, obtained by adding certain simple universal axioms for $\exp$, namely, $$\exp(1) = 2, \quad \exp(x + y) = \exp(x) \exp(y), \quad \exp(x) > x.$$ We prove that this theory is $\Pi_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{IOpen}$ and $\forall$-conservative over the theory of discretely ordered $\mathbb Z$-semirings. This result extends a result of A. Wilkie and provides a partial answer to a question of E. Je\v{r}\'abek concerning the strength of the theory of exponential integer parts.

item.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
item.description: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. item.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
item.description: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act. In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties. We then show that these allocation constraints cannot be resolved within a single layer of control. Instead, they propagate across the system, interacting with execution atomicity, state enforcement, and behavioral drift. This leads to a multi-scale governance structure composed of four orthogonal dimensions: temporal (atomicity), state (enforcement), behavioral (drift monitoring), and population (allocation).
